about.title: Your reliable partner since 1985
text: Since 1985, Air Tech of Houston AC & Plumbing has delivered home comfort work to homeowners throughout the Houston area. What began as an HVAC company has grown into a full-service provider covering heating, cooling, electrical, plumbing, generators, drain cleaning and indoor air quality, all from one team.

From fast repairs and routine maintenance to complete system replacements and new installations, the technicians are trained, certified and equipped for everything from air conditioning and heating systems to whole-home generators, electrical upgrades, plumbing repairs and indoor air quality work.

The industry keeps changing, which is why Air Tech keeps investing in training so technicians stay current with the technology, codes and best practices. That is what makes the difference between a lasting solution and a temporary fix.

Every service is backed by written satisfaction guarantees, and the Shield of Protection membership plan adds priority scheduling, discounts and preventative maintenance for homeowners who would rather stay ahead of problems than react to them.

faqs.q: How often should I have my HVAC system maintained?
faqs.a: Twice a year. AC tune-ups in the spring before Houston's heat and humidity arrive, and heating maintenance in the fall before you actually need it. If you would rather stop thinking about it, the Shield of Protection membership handles the scheduling for you.

faqs.q: What does preventative maintenance actually include?
faqs.a: A technician inspects the fans, compressors, coils, refrigerant lines, electrical connections, drain lines, ductwork and furnace components. The point is to find the small problems while they are still small, before they turn into an expensive repair in the middle of a heat wave.

faqs.q: What is a SEER rating and does it matter?
faqs.a: SEER stands for Seasonal Energy Efficiency Ratio, and it measures how much cooling you get for every dollar of electricity. A higher number means lower bills. Modern systems start around 14 SEER, and we back new installations with a 30% utility savings guarantee.

faqs.q: How often should I change my air filter?
faqs.a: A standard one-inch filter usually needs replacing every 30 days. Thicker media filters can go 60 to 90 days. Shorten the interval if you have pets or anyone in the house has allergies.

faqs.q: What should I set my thermostat to?
faqs.a: Whatever you are comfortable with. For efficiency, 78 degrees while you are home and higher while you are out is the usual advice, and a smart thermostat handles the switching for you.

faqs.q: How often should I clean my AC drain line?
faqs.a: Once a month is a good habit. Flush it with a mix of equal parts warm water and white vinegar.

faqs.q: How long should my HVAC system last?
faqs.a: It depends on the equipment, how it was installed and how well it has been maintained. Generally a well-maintained system in the Houston area runs 12 to 18 years. Between the long summers, the humidity and the occasional hard freeze, regular maintenance is the single biggest factor in getting the most life out of it.

faqs.q: How do I know what HVAC system is right for my home?
faqs.a: Bigger is not better. An oversized system short-cycles, wears out faster and never properly dehumidifies the house. An undersized one runs constantly and still cannot keep up. We do a full in-home load analysis covering square footage, insulation, window placement, ceiling height and duct layout before recommending anything.

faqs.q: Do you give quotes over the phone?
faqs.a: No. A phone quote is either too low, so you are surprised at the door, or padded to protect us, so you overpay. We send a technician, they assess what is actually going on, and give you a clear price before touching anything. You decide whether to move forward.

faqs.q: What is a slab leak and how do I know if I have one?
faqs.a: A slab leak is a leak in the water lines that run beneath the concrete foundation, and they are more common in the Houston area than most homeowners realise. Signs include warm spots on the floor, the sound of running water when everything is off, an unexplained rise in the water bill, or cracks in flooring or walls. Left alone they cause serious foundation damage.

faqs.q: Do you warranty your plumbing work?
faqs.a: Yes. The terms vary by the type of service, and we go through them with you before the work starts rather than after.

faqs.q: Why does my circuit breaker keep tripping?
faqs.a: Usually overload. High-draw appliances like a microwave, toaster and hair dryer running at once will do it. Try unplugging everything on that circuit and resetting the breaker. If it holds, the problem is likely one of the devices. If it trips again with nothing plugged in, there is a wiring issue and you need an electrician.

faqs.q: I lost power to part of my house. What should I check first?
faqs.a: Look for a tripped GFCI outlet with a reset button on it, usually in a bathroom, kitchen, garage or outside. Then check the breaker panel for a flipped breaker. If neither explains it, call us.

faqs.q: What is a GFCI and why does mine keep tripping?
faqs.a: A GFCI, or ground fault circuit interrupter, watches the flow of electricity and cuts it off the instant it detects an imbalance. Nuisance tripping usually comes down to a failing appliance on the circuit, moisture, or a GFCI that has simply worn out.

faqs.q: Can I replace a circuit breaker or outlet myself?
faqs.a: We strongly recommend you do not. The panel is energised even when the main breaker is off, and touching the wrong part can cause serious injury or start a fire.

faqs.q: Why does half my house have no power?
faqs.a: That usually means a lost leg, where one of the two 120-volt lines feeding the house has a bad connection. If the fault is on the utility's side of the meter they will test and repair it at no cost to you. If it is at your meter or panel, it needs a licensed electrician.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a standby generator and a portable one?
faqs.a: A portable generator runs on gasoline, has to be started by hand and needs to stay well outside the house. A standby generator is permanently installed, connected to the natural gas or propane line and tied into the panel, so it senses the outage and starts within seconds on its own.

faqs.q: Is the Shield of Protection worth it if my system is newer?
faqs.a: Yes. Manufacturer warranties generally require documented maintenance to stay valid, so the tune-ups protect the coverage you already paid for. The free diagnostic fee on its own offsets much of the membership, and the yearly loyalty credit builds toward the eventual replacement.

faqs.q: Are your technicians licensed?
faqs.a: Yes. Every technician is licensed, background checked and holds the credentials required for their trade. Our electricians and plumbers hold state licenses, our HVAC technicians are EPA certified, we are fully insured, and we carry a BBB A+ rating.

faqs.q: Do you offer financing?
faqs.a: Yes. A new HVAC system, a whole-home generator or a full repipe is not a small purchase, so we offer financing through Synchrony, Wells Fargo Home Projects and Service Finance. Terms vary by project and all options are subject to credit approval.
